# DSR-1.2 Hook request identity clarification

Status: Approved (2026-10-01); implementation verification is recorded in [the construction ledger](../sources/2026-10-01-offline-construction.md).

## Authority

The operator approved the recommendation with “do the recommendation” and required documentation evidence and reasoning. This clarifies DSR-1.2, not its real model proof obligations. Paid calls remain disabled, contact deferred, and Phase 2 closed.

## Documented behavior

On resume, the engine invokes PreToolUse again for the pending request. The hook may defer again. The documented eventual allow path executes the tool; it does not establish our host supplied result mechanism. Batching ignores deferral. [Official hook reference, read 2026-10-01](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#defer-a-tool-call-for-later).

## Approved contract and engineering reasoning

Before a stop, the first new effect or ask request claims one paused slot and returns defer. An identical reannouncement returns defer without replacing that slot. Every different call, including reads, is denied after a pause. Every call is denied after stop. Skill remains denied until DSR-1.5 supplies its validator. An already answered ID returns defer without acquiring a new slot under the existing resume mechanism.

Binding the paused slot to ID, exact name and canonical JSON inputs is our additional engineering check, not a vendor requirement. An ID alone cannot distinguish an unchanged callback from a different command or payload using that ID. Canonical object ordering accepts equivalent JSON objects while changed values remain distinct. Exclusive marker creation prevents a second request from replacing the first. Invalid markers fail closed. The runner checks the returned deferred request against the marker before checkpointing, so the accepted hook request and the persisted request cannot silently differ.

This is request identity within one segment, not semantic effect deduplication. Already answered IDs are not yet bound to a durable name and input ledger across segments. That gap remains for later resume validation. The hook relies on the runner's private, validated policy file; it is not a tamper proof broker or process isolation boundary.

## Evidence and limits

The inherited hook already allows repeated deferral by paused ID: [pinned source, lines 70 to 80](https://github.com/osamastro7-droid/ai-integrations/blob/69f5497d3d3dec7ad3269c72ff266c2931c9f379/python/claude_agent_sdk/src/temporalio/claude_agent_sdk/_defer_hook.py#L70-L80). The wording correction preserves that protocol while strengthening policy request identity. Offline tests cover exact repetition, changed name and input, object ordering, corrupt markers, concurrent different requests, stop priority, and checkpoint mismatch refusal. The construction ledger owns executed results.

DSR-1.3 and DSR-1.4 still require real model resume and preventive backstop proof. This decision does not retire engine assumptions, prove batch safety, or authorize allow, new tools, paid calls or effect execution.
